definition: ARTICLE used to specify a particular noun, indicating it is definite, previously mentioned, or contextually clear; used with singular or plural nouns to denote uniqueness (e.g., 'the sun'), generalization (e.g., 'the tiger is fierce'), or in superlatives and fixed expressions.
example: The sun, the only star in our solar system, is the brightest object in the sky.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating movement toward a place, person, or thing; denotes purpose, recipient, or result. As an INFINITIVE MARKER, it precedes a verb to express intention or purpose. Also used in comparisons (e.g., 'superior to') and ratios (e.g., 'two to one').
example: She traveled to Paris to learn French, where the ratio of students to teachers is low.

definition: CONJUNCTION connecting words, phrases, or clauses, indicating addition, sequence, or result; also used for emphasis (e.g., 'and how') or in lists.
example: She bought apples, bananas, and oranges, and she ate them all in one day.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating possession, origin, relationship, or composition; expresses part of a whole (e.g., 'piece of cake'), material (e.g., 'made of wood'), or cause (e.g., 'die of hunger').
example: The crown of the king, made of gold, was a symbol of power.

definition: INDEFINITE ARTICLE used before singular countable nouns with consonant sounds, indicating a non-specific item; also in expressions like 'a few' or 'a lot'.
example: I saw a cat in the garden, and it was a beautiful one.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating location within a space, period of time, or condition; denotes inclusion, state, or method. As an ADVERB, it signifies being present, indoors, or a specific stage or position.
example: She found her keys in the drawer, and decided to stay in for the evening due to the rain.

definition: PRONOUN referring to a male person or animal previously mentioned or easily identified, used as the subject of a verb. It can also refer to a person of unspecified gender in a general sense, though 'they' is often preferred.
example: He decided to visit the library, as he loves reading books.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN used to refer to a specific thing or person previously mentioned, known, or understood, typically more distant than 'this'. As a CONJUNCTION, it introduces a subordinate clause. As an ADVERB, it means 'to such an extent'.
example: That book, which I read last week, was so good that I couldn't put it down.

definition: PRONOUN referring to the person or people being addressed, used as both subject and object. It can be singular or plural, and also used informally to refer to people in general.
example: You should always try your best, and remember that you are capable of great things.

definition: DETERMINER or POSSESSIVE PRONOUN indicating belonging to or associated with a male person or animal previously mentioned. As a pronoun, it can stand alone, replacing 'his + noun'.
example: He showed me his new car, which was parked right next to his, referring to a friend's car.

definition: VERB, the past tense singular form of 'to be', used to describe a state or condition that existed in the past, or to form the passive voice.
example: The weather was beautiful yesterday, and she was very happy to be outdoors.

definition: PRONOUN referring to a non-human thing, animal, or abstract concept previously mentioned or understood, used as the subject or object of a verb. It also functions as a dummy subject (e.g., 'It is raining').
example: It is raining heavily outside, so I think it's better to stay inside.

definition: VERB, the third person singular present tense form of 'to be', used to describe a current state, identity, or quality, or to form continuous tenses and the passive voice.
example: The sky is blue today, and it is a wonderful day for a walk.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating purpose, recipient, duration, or a specific reason. As a CONJUNCTION, it means 'because' or 'since', providing a reason for something.
example: This gift is for you, for I know how much you appreciate thoughtful gestures.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating accompaniment, possession, means, or manner. It shows connection, having something, using something, or doing something in a particular way. As an ADVERB, it can mean together or along.
example: She traveled with her friends, painting with watercolors, and finished the project with great success.

definition: CONJUNCTION meaning 'at the same time that' or 'because'; PREPOSITION meaning 'in the capacity of'; ADVERB meaning 'to the same degree' or 'for example'.
example: As a lawyer, she advised her client as thoroughly as possible, knowing he had to act fast as time was running out.

definition: VERB, the past tense and past participle form of 'to have', indicating possession or experience in the past. As an auxiliary, it forms past perfect tenses.
example: He had finished his homework before dinner, and later realized he had a lot of free time.

definition: PRONOUN referring to two or more people, animals, or things previously mentioned or easily identified, used as the subject of a verb. It can also refer to a single person whose gender is unknown or not specified.
example: They arrived late, but they still managed to enjoy the entire concert.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating position above and supported by something, attachment, or a particular day/date. As an ADVERB, it means in operation or progress.
example: The book is on the table, and the television is on, playing my favorite show.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN used to refer to a specific thing or person close at hand, recently mentioned, or about to be mentioned. It denotes proximity or immediate relevance.
example: This is the house I was telling you about; I bought this last month.

definition: DETERMINER belonging to or associated with the people or things previously mentioned or understood. It is the possessive form of 'they'.
example: The students submitted their assignments, and their teacher praised their hard work.

definition: DETERMINER belonging to or associated with the person or people being addressed. It is the possessive form of 'you'.
example: Please bring your books tomorrow, and make sure your homework is complete.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating proximity, means, or agency; meaning 'next to', 'through the use of', or 'performed by'. As an ADVERB, it means past or near.
example: The package was delivered by hand, and I walked right by the old market.

definition: CONJUNCTION introducing a contrast or exception; PREPOSITION meaning 'except'; ADVERB meaning 'only' or 'no more than'.
example: She wanted to go, but she was too tired, and everyone but her decided to stay.

definition: VERB denoting existence, state, or quality; used as a linking verb or an auxiliary verb to form various tenses (e.g., continuous, passive voice) or express obligation.
example: To be or not to be, that is the question; one must be careful with their words.

definition: AUXILIARY VERB used to form the conditional mood, express a polite request, a habitual past action, or the past form of 'will' in reported speech.
example: She would often visit her grandmother when she was younger, and he said he would help.

definition: ADVERB used to make a statement negative, indicating denial, refusal, or absence. It often precedes the verb or an auxiliary verb.
example: He did not want to go to the party, as it was not his kind of event.

definition: PRONOUN referring to a male person or animal previously mentioned or easily identified, used as the object of a verb or preposition.
example: I gave him the book, and she waved at him from across the street.

definition: PRONOUN referring to a female person or animal as the object of a verb or preposition. As a DETERMINER, it indicates possession by a female.
example: I saw her at the park, and her dog was running happily beside her.

definition: VERB, the second person singular present, and first, second, third person plural present form of 'to be', used to describe a current state, identity, or quality, or to form continuous tenses and the passive voice.
example: You are very kind, and we are all proud of your achievements.

definition: PRONOUN referring to two or more people, animals, or things previously mentioned or easily identified, used as the object of a verb or preposition.
example: I gave them the keys, and the teacher assigned them a new project.

definition: CONJUNCTION used to connect alternatives or options, indicating a choice between two or more possibilities. It can also imply a rephrasing or explanation.
example: Do you want coffee or tea, or perhaps you'd prefer water?

definition: PREPOSITION indicating specific location, time, or state; used to denote a precise point (e.g., 'at the corner'), a particular time (e.g., 'at noon'), or an activity (e.g., 'at work').
example: We met at the coffee shop at 3 PM, and he looked at me curiously.

definition: AUXILIARY VERB used to form the future tense, express a strong intention, or indicate probability. As a NOUN, it refers to a strong desire or determination, or a legal document stating one's wishes for property.
example: I will meet you tomorrow, and he expressed his strong will to succeed despite the challenges.

definition: INDEFINITE ARTICLE used before singular countable nouns beginning with a vowel sound, indicating a non-specific item, or in phrases like 'an hour'.
example: She ate an apple and an orange for breakfast, enjoying an amazing start to her day.

definition: PRONOUN referring to a female person or animal previously mentioned or easily identified, used as the subject of a verb.
example: She sings beautifully, and she is also an excellent dancer.

definition: VERB indicating possession, experience, or obligation. As an auxiliary, it forms perfect tenses. It can also mean to experience or to consume.
example: I have a new car, and I have just finished reading a great book.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating origin, source, or starting point in space or time; also used to show distance, cause, or a change of state.
example: She received a letter from her friend who lives far from here, and the train departs from platform 5.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN meaning the whole quantity or extent of; every single one. As an ADVERB, it means entirely or completely.
example: All the students passed the exam, and she was all alone in the large house.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN indicating a greater quantity, number, or degree. As an ADVERB, it means to a greater extent. As an ADJECTIVE, it is the comparative form of 'much' or 'many'.
example: She wanted more cake, and he felt more tired than usual after the long journey.

definition: NUMBER representing a single unit or item. As a PRONOUN, it refers to a person or thing previously mentioned or generally. As an ADJECTIVE, it indicates a single item.
example: She picked one apple, and this is the one I wanted.

definition: INTERROGATIVE/RELATIVE PRONOUN used to ask about or refer to a person or people. It serves as the subject of a clause or sentence.
example: Who is coming to the party, and she is the person who organized the event?

definition: PRONOUN referring to the speaker/writer and one or more other people, used as the subject of a verb.
example: We are going to the beach, and we should leave soon.

definition: NOUN plural of 'person', referring to human beings in general, or the members of a particular nation, community, or ethnic group.
example: Many people gathered in the park to protest, and the local people are very friendly.

definition: VERB, the past tense plural form of 'to be', or the past tense second person singular form of 'to be' (informal), used to describe a state or condition that existed in the past.
example: They were happy to see us, and you were always so kind.

definition: CONJUNCTION introducing a conditional clause, indicating a condition or supposition. It can also introduce an indirect question or express doubt.
example: If it rains, we will stay inside, and I wonder if he's coming.

definition: INTERROGATIVE PRONOUN/DETERMINER used to ask for information about something or to specify something. As an ADVERB, it means 'to what extent'.
example: What do you want to eat, and I don't know what happened next.

definition: PRONOUN referring to the speaker or writer, used as the subject of a verb. It is always capitalized.
example: I believe I can fly, and I also love to read.

definition: ADVERB/CONJUNCTION used to ask or state the time at which something happens. As a PRONOUN, it refers to a time.
example: When will you arrive, and she was happy when she heard the news.

definition: ADVERB meaning 'to such a great extent' or 'very'. As a CONJUNCTION, it introduces a consequence or result.
example: The movie was so long, so we decided to leave early.

definition: AUXILIARY VERB, the past form of 'can', used to express possibility, ability in the past, or a polite request.
example: She could run very fast when she was young, and I wish I could help you more.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating movement towards the inside of something, or a change of state/condition. It also denotes division or impact.
example: He walked into the room, and the caterpillar turned into a beautiful butterfly.

definition: AUXILIARY VERB expressing ability, possibility, or permission. As a NOUN, it refers to a metal container.
example: I can speak French fluently, and he opened a can of beans for dinner.

definition: ADVERB/PREPOSITION indicating movement to a higher level or position. As an ADJECTIVE, it means elevated. As a VERB, it means to raise. As a NOUN, it can refer to an upward movement.
example: She looked up at the stars, and prices went up significantly last month.

definition: DETERMINER indicating absence or negation; ADVERB used to express a negative answer or refusal. As an INTERJECTION, it's a direct denial. As a NOUN, it refers to a negative vote.
example: There is no sugar left, and he said "no" to the offer, making it a clear no from his side.

definition: ADVERB/PREPOSITION indicating movement away from the inside of something. As an ADJECTIVE, it means absent or extinguished. As a NOUN, it refers to an exit. As a VERB, it means to reveal.
example: She went out to play, and the fire went out suddenly.

definition: NOUN indicating the indefinite continued progress of existence and events, a specific moment, or a duration. As a VERB, it means to measure or set the duration of something.
example: What time is it, and we had a great time at the party?

definition: NOUN referring to the ability to do something, control over others, or a form of energy. As a VERB, it means to supply with energy or enable movement.
example: The country's leader had immense power, and the new engine will power the entire factory.

definition: INTERROGATIVE/RELATIVE PRONOUN/DETERMINER used to ask about or specify one or more items from a limited set. It can refer to things, animals, or ideas.
example: Which book do you prefer, and the house, which was built in 1900, is now for sale.

definition: VERB meaning to create, cause to be, or bring about. As a NOUN, it refers to a brand or type of product.
example: She will make a cake for the party, and he tried to make her laugh.

definition: AUXILIARY VERB used to form questions, negatives, or for emphasis. As a MAIN VERB, it means to perform an action or accomplish something. As a NOUN, it can refer to a social gathering.
example: What do you want to do today, and he always does his best work in the morning.

definition: ADVERB meaning solely or exclusively. As an ADJECTIVE, it means unique or single. As a CONJUNCTION, it introduces a condition or reservation.
example: He was the only person who knew the secret, and she only eats vegetables.

definition: CONJUNCTION/PREPOSITION used to introduce the second part of a comparison, indicating difference in degree or amount.
example: She is taller than her brother, and I prefer coffee rather than tea.

definition: NOUN referring to a method, route, or particular style. As an ADVERB (informal), it means 'far' or 'very'.
example: What's the best way to get there, and she has a unique way of looking at things.

definition: ADVERB indicating a place or position; also used as an introductory word in sentences (e.g., 'there is'). As a PRONOUN, it replaces a place. As an INTERJECTION, it expresses satisfaction or concern.
example: Let's go over there, and there are many people waiting.

definition: ADJECTIVE meaning belonging to oneself or itself. As a VERB, it means to possess something. As a PRONOUN, it emphasizes possession.
example: She has her own business, and he hopes to own a house one day.

definition: NOUN referring to an adult male human being. It can also refer to a human being regardless of gender, or humanity in general. As a VERB, it means to staff or operate.
example: The man walked into the room, and the team will need to man the fort against invaders.

definition: ADVERB meaning 'at that time', 'after that', or 'in that case'. As an ADJECTIVE, it means existing at that time. As a NOUN, it refers to that particular time.
example: First, we'll eat, and then we'll watch a movie.

definition: ADJECTIVE meaning different from one already mentioned or implied; additional. As a PRONOUN, it refers to the remaining or additional people/things. As an ADVERB, it implies differently.
example: Do you have any other questions, or should we discuss the other option?

definition: DETERMINER belonging to or associated with the speaker and one or more other people. It is the possessive form of 'we'.
example: This is our house, and we are proud of our team's performance.

definition: PREPOSITION meaning 'concerning' or 'on the subject of'. As an ADVERB, it means 'approximately' or 'nearly'.
example: We talked about our plans for the future, and it's about five o'clock.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN meaning the greatest in quantity, amount, or degree. As an ADVERB, it forms the superlative of adjectives and adverbs.
example: Most people enjoy music, and she is the most talented singer I know.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN indicating an unspecified amount or number; a certain but not large quantity. As an ADVERB (informal), it can mean 'to some extent'.
example: I need some sugar for this recipe, and some of the students arrived late.

definition: ADVERB used to ask about the way or manner something is done, its condition, or extent. As a CONJUNCTION, it introduces a clause of manner or extent.
example: How do you feel today, and I wonder how he managed to finish so quickly.

definition: NOUN referring to the state of being alive; the period between birth and death; or the existence of an individual or species. It can also mean vitality or an aspect of human existence.
example: She has lived a long and happy life, full of adventures and meaningful experiences.

definition: PREPOSITION meaning similar to or characteristic of. As a VERB, it means to find pleasant or agreeable. As an ADJECTIVE/ADVERB (informal), it introduces an example or approximation. As a NOUN, it refers to something similar.
example: She likes to read books like detective novels, and he looks just like his father.

definition: AUXILIARY VERB indicating necessity, obligation, or strong probability. As a NOUN, it refers to something that is necessary or required.
example: You must complete your homework, and it's a must-see movie for anyone interested in history.

definition: ADVERB meaning at no time; not ever. It indicates complete absence or negation of an action or state.
example: I will never forget that day, and she never complains about anything.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN referring to things or people that are plural and close at hand, recently mentioned, or about to be mentioned. It is the plural form of 'this'.
example: These books are mine, and I bought these last week at the market.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN meaning of the type previously mentioned or about to be mentioned; of a particular kind. As an ADVERB, it emphasizes a quality.
example: I've never seen such a beautiful sunset, and she has such talent.

definition: DETERMINER, the possessive form of 'it', indicating belonging to or associated with a thing, animal, or abstract concept. Do not confuse with 'it's' (it is/it has).
example: The tree lost its leaves in autumn, and the company is known for its innovative products.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating position above, covering, or across; ADVERB meaning finished or in excess. As an ADJECTIVE, it means completed.
example: The plane flew over the city, and the game was finally over after extra time.

definition: VERB to perceive with the eyes, understand, or experience. As a NOUN (informal), it can refer to a bishop's area of authority.
example: I can see the mountains from here, and I see what you mean.

definition: ADVERB used to emphasize something unexpected or surprising; ADJECTIVE meaning flat, smooth, or equal. As a VERB, it means to make equal.
example: Even though it was raining, they still went for a walk, and they managed to even the score.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN referring to one, some, or all indiscriminately, typically used in questions or negative statements. As an ADVERB, it means 'at all' or 'to any extent'.
example: Do you have any questions, and I don't have any money left.

definition: VERB, the third person singular present tense form of 'to have', indicating possession or experience. As an auxiliary, it forms perfect tenses.
example: She has a beautiful garden, and he has finished his work.

definition: ADJECTIVE/ADVERB indicating preceding all others in time, order, or importance. As a NOUN, it refers to the beginning or the initial position.
example: This is the first time I've been here, and she finished first in the race.

definition: VERB, the past participle of 'to be', used to form perfect and passive tenses, indicating a state or action that has occurred at some point or continued up to a certain time.
example: I have been to Paris many times, and the book has been read by millions.

definition: REFLEXIVE/EMPHATIC PRONOUN referring to a male person or animal previously mentioned, used when the object of a verb or preposition is the same as the subject, or for emphasis.
example: He built the house himself, and he often talks to himself when he's thinking.

definition: PREPOSITION indicating movement from one side or end to the other, or by means of. As an ADVERB, it means from beginning to end. As an ADJECTIVE, it means finished.
example: The light passed through the window, and we worked through the night to finish the project.

definition: NOUN referring to a state of armed conflict between different countries or groups, or a sustained effort to combat something. As a VERB, it means to engage in conflict.
example: The country declared war, and they prepared to war against poverty.

definition: ADJECTIVE meaning not existing before, recently made or acquired, or unfamiliar. It implies a change from a previous state or a beginning.
example: She bought a new dress for the party, and they explored a new strategy for the business.

definition: ADJECTIVE meaning considerable in amount, extent, or intensity; significant, excellent, or important. As an ADVERB, it emphasizes a quality. As a NOUN, it refers to a distinguished person.
example: He achieved great success in his career, and it was a great day for a picnic.

definition: ADVERB meaning 'to a greater extent than is desirable, permissible, or possible'; also meaning 'in addition' or 'also'.
example: It's too hot to go outside, and I want to come too.

definition: VERB, the past tense and past participle of 'make', meaning created, caused to be, or produced.
example: She made a delicious cake, and the house was made of bricks.

definition: ADVERB meaning at the present time or moment; immediately. As a CONJUNCTION, it introduces a reason or consequence. As a NOUN, it refers to the present moment.
example: We need to leave now, or we'll be late.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN meaning a large amount of something (uncountable). As an ADVERB, it means to a great extent or a lot.
example: I don't have much time, but I appreciate your help very much.

definition: NOUN referring to activity involving mental or physical effort done in order to achieve a purpose or result, especially as paid employment. As a VERB, it means to perform a task.
example: I have a lot of work to do today, and the machine doesn't work properly.

definition: PRONOUN referring to an unspecified thing or amount. As an ADVERB (informal), it indicates an unspecified degree or extent.
example: There's something in my eye, and I need to tell you something important.

definition: PREPOSITION meaning later than, behind, or in pursuit of. As an ADVERB, it means later in time. As a CONJUNCTION, it introduces a clause indicating a subsequent event.
example: We went for a walk after dinner, and he arrived shortly after.

definition: PRONOUN The objective case of 'we', referring to the speaker and one or more other people collectively. It functions as the object of a verb or preposition, or sometimes as a subjective complement in informal contexts. It can also indicate belonging or relationship.
example: They invited us to the party, which was very kind of them to do for us.

definition: AUXILIARY VERB, MAIN VERB (past tense of 'do') The past tense form of the verb 'do'. It is used as an auxiliary verb to form past simple questions and negative statements, or for emphasis. As a main verb, it refers to performing an action or task, or creating something.
example: She did her homework before going out, and later I did my part to help.

definition: NOUN A plural unit of time representing a period of 365 or 366 days, typically from January 1 to December 31, corresponding to one revolution of the Earth around the sun. It can also refer to age or a long period of time.
example: We have been friends for many years, and these years have been full of cherished memories.

definition: NOUN The Earth, its inhabitants, or the whole of existence and reality. It can also refer to a particular country, period, or group of people, or a distinct sphere of activity, knowledge, or experience.
example: The entire world watched as the astronaut orbited the Earth, a truly global event.

definition: DETERMINER, PRONOUN, ADJECTIVE A quantifier indicating a large indefinite number or amount. As a determiner, it precedes plural countable nouns. As a pronoun, it replaces such nouns. As an adjective, it describes something as numerous.
example: Many people attended the concert, and many were surprised by the unexpected rain.

definition: VERB To lay hold of something with one's hands; to get possession of. Also means to transport or carry, to accept or receive, to consume, or to interpret or understand. Can imply capture or removal.
example: Please take your belongings with you when you leave, and take care on the journey home.

definition: ADVERB Frequently or on many occasions; repeatedly. It indicates a high frequency of an action or event, though not necessarily always, and can suggest regularity.
example: She often visits her grandparents, but not as often as she would like to.

definition: NOUN (plural of 'man') The plural form of 'man', referring to adult male human beings. It can also refer to people in general, especially when distinguishing from women, or to members of a particular group or profession.
example: The men gathered at the town hall to discuss the new regulations, and these men represented diverse views.

definition: VERB To obtain, receive, or acquire something. It can also mean to reach a particular state or condition, to move or travel, to understand, or to cause something to happen. Very versatile with many phrasal verbs.
example: I need to get my keys before I can get to the office and get some work done.

definition: NOUN The male ruler of an independent state, especially one who inherits the position by right of birth. Also, a person or thing preeminent in a particular sphere, or a playing card/chess piece.
example: The wise king ruled his kingdom justly for many years, earning the respect of his people.

definition: NOUN An organized military force equipped for fighting on land. It can also refer to a large number of people or things, especially one organized for a particular purpose or task, indicating a collective group.
example: The country's army prepared for the upcoming defense, a formidable force ready to protect the nation.

definition: ADVERB, NOUN, ADJECTIVE, VERB ADVERB: To or toward the rear; in return; in a previous time. NOUN: The rear surface of the human body or an object. ADJECTIVE: Located at the rear. VERB: To move backward or support someone/something.
example: He went back to his room to get his wallet from the back pocket of his trousers.

definition: DETERMINER, PRONOUN The plural form of 'that'. As a determiner, it refers to specific people or things previously mentioned or understood from context, indicating a greater distance or difference than 'these'. As a pronoun, it replaces such nouns.
example: Those books on the top shelf are the ones I recommended, and those will help you a lot.

definition: PREPOSITION, CONJUNCTION, ADVERB PREPOSITION: Earlier than (in time); in front of (in position). CONJUNCTION: Prior to the time that. ADVERB: At an earlier time; previously.
example: Always check the expiration date before you buy food, especially before large gatherings.

definition: VERB To move or travel towards a speaker or a specified place or point; to arrive. Can also mean to reach a particular state or condition, or to happen or occur, implying an arrival or transformation.
example: Please come to the meeting on time, and come prepared with your ideas.

definition: ADVERB On every occasion; at all times. It denotes continuous presence, repetition, or an unchangeable truth. Can also imply persistence or a habitual action.
example: She always remembers my birthday, and she always sends a thoughtful gift.

definition: ADVERB In addition; too; besides. It is used to include an additional item or idea, often emphasizing similarity or further relevance to what has already been stated.
example: He is a talented musician, and he is also an excellent painter.

definition: PRONOUN The reflexive form of 'you', used when 'you' is the object of a verb or preposition and also its subject. It can also be used for emphasis, meaning 'you, and nobody else'.
example: You should be proud of yourself for completing the marathon, and you yourself know how much effort that took.

definition: ADVERB, CONJUNCTION, NOUN ADVERB: On one occasion only; at some time in the past; formerly. CONJUNCTION: As soon as; when. NOUN: A single occasion or time, signifying singularity or past occurrence.
example: Once upon a time, there was a king who ruled wisely, and once he made a promise, he always kept it.

definition: PREPOSITION In opposition to; contrary to the interest or advantage of. It can also indicate contact, resistance, or comparison (e.g., 'against the odds'), showing an opposing force or proximity.
example: The team played well against a strong opponent, despite the odds being against them.

definition: NOUN, VERB (present participle of 'be') NOUN: Existence; the nature or essence of a person or thing; a living creature. VERB: Present participle of 'be', used to form continuous tenses or as a gerund.
example: Human beings are complex creatures, and simply being present can sometimes be enough.

definition: ADJECTIVE, NOUN ADJECTIVE: Having or showing a friendly, generous, and considerate nature. NOUN: A class or category of people or things with shared characteristics; a type, indicating classification.
example: She is a very kind person, always ready to help others, and this kind of generosity is rare.

definition: NOUN, VERB NOUN: The element of a person that enables them to be aware of the world and their experiences, to think, feel, and make decisions; intellect. VERB: To object to, care about, or pay attention to something.
example: Keep an open mind when you explore new ideas, and don't mind if others disagree initially.

definition: NUMBER, ADJECTIVE, NOUN The number equivalent to the sum of one and one; one more than one. As an adjective, it precedes a noun to indicate quantity. As a noun, it refers to the digit or quantity itself.
example: We have two tickets for the concert, enough for two people to attend.

definition: NOUN A plan of action or policy designed to achieve a major or overall aim. It involves careful planning and execution, especially in military, business, or political contexts, to achieve specific goals.
example: The company developed a new marketing strategy to reach a wider audience, and this strategy proved successful.

definition: CONJUNCTION For the reason that; introduces a clause giving the cause or reason for something. It explains why an action is performed or why a situation exists, providing justification.
example: She was late because her car broke down, and because of the traffic, she missed the first part of the meeting.

definition: VERB, NOUN VERB: To experience an emotion or sensation; to perceive by touch; to have a strong belief or impression. NOUN: An act of touching or sensing; an impression or atmosphere.
example: I feel a sense of joy when I see my family, and the smooth feel of silk is always pleasant.

definition: PRONOUN, NOUN (plural of 'other') PRONOUN: Other people or things. NOUN: Persons or things distinct from those already mentioned or known. Often refers to the rest of a group, indicating additional entities.
example: She cared deeply about others, always putting the needs of others before her own.

definition: NOUN, VERB NOUN: An intense feeling of deep affection; a great interest and pleasure in something. VERB: To feel deep affection for someone or something; to like or enjoy greatly.
example: Their love for each other was evident, and they truly loved spending time together.

definition: NOUN A person who is actively opposed or hostile to someone or something. It can also refer to a force or thing that harms or threatens, such as a disease or bad habit, representing opposition.
example: The general knew his enemy's tactics well, making him a formidable opponent.

definition: NOUN The system of rules that a particular country or community recognizes as regulating the actions of its members and may enforce by the imposition of penalties. Also, a statement of fact deduced from observation.
example: Everyone must abide by the law, as it ensures order and justice in society.

definition: VERB, NOUN VERB: To move from one place or point to another; to proceed. Can also mean to function, to elapse (of time), or to become. NOUN: An attempt or turn, indicating movement or action.
example: We decided to go for a walk in the park, and it was a good go despite the slight drizzle.

definition: DETERMINER, PRONOUN, ADJECTIVE A small number of; not many. As a determiner, it precedes plural countable nouns. As a pronoun, it replaces such nouns. As an adjective, it describes something as being small in number.
example: Only a few students understood the complex concept, and a few of them asked for clarification.

definition: PREPOSITION, ADVERB PREPOSITION: Not having, using, or doing something; in the absence of. ADVERB: On the outside; lacking something. Often implies a state of being deprived or an absence.
example: He left the house without saying a word, and without a doubt, he was upset.

definition: ADVERB, CONJUNCTION, PRONOUN ADVERB: In or at what place or position; to or in what place. CONJUNCTION: In or at the place that; in a situation or case in which. PRONOUN: What place.
example: Do you know where the nearest post office is, and where we can find a good coffee shop?

definition: MODAL VERB Used to express possibility or permission. It indicates that something is likely to happen, or that someone is allowed to do something. Also used in wishes or formal requests.
example: You may leave when you finish your work, and it may rain later this afternoon.

definition: ADVERB, ADJECTIVE, INTERJECTION, NOUN, VERB ADVERB: In a good or satisfactory way. ADJECTIVE: In good health. INTERJECTION: Expressing surprise or resignation. NOUN: A source of water; a shaft. VERB: To rise to the surface and flow out.
example: She performed very well in the exam, and thankfully, she is feeling well after her recovery.

definition: NOUN A period of 24 hours, especially from midnight to midnight. It can also refer to the time between sunrise and sunset, or a specific day of the week, or an era.
example: Today is a beautiful day for a picnic, and she plans to make the most of her day off.

definition: VERB To begin to be; to grow into a particular state or condition. It indicates a process of change or transformation, often resulting in a new identity or status.
example: He hopes to become a doctor one day, and with hard work, his dreams will become a reality.

definition: VERB, NOUN VERB: To discover or perceive something or someone by chance, search, or exploration; to realize or determine. NOUN: A discovery, especially of something valuable, indicating a successful search.
example: I hope to find my lost keys soon, and the archaeological team made an amazing find.

definition: ADVERB, PREPOSITION, ADJECTIVE, NOUN, VERB ADVERB/PREPOSITION: To a lower level or position. ADJECTIVE: Directed or moving downward; depressed. NOUN: Soft fine feathers or hair. VERB: To consume quickly; to defeat.
example: He looked down the street, feeling a bit down after the news.

definition: NOUN (plural of 'thing') Objects, matters, or possessions. Refers to items that are not living or are abstract concepts, or to general circumstances and affairs, denoting various elements or situations.
example: There are so many things to do today, from organizing my things to finishing reports.

definition: PREPOSITION, ADVERB PREPOSITION: On every side of; surrounding. ADVERB: On every side; in a circle; approximately. Also, in or to many places, or present in a place.
example: We walked around the park, looking at all the beautiful flowers around us.

definition: VERB (past tense of 'begin') The past tense of 'begin'. It means to start doing something, to take the first step, or to come into existence, indicating the initiation of an action or state.
example: The concert began exactly at 7 PM, and the rain began shortly after.

definition: VERB, NOUN VERB: To hand over something to someone; to provide or supply; to bestow or grant. Can also mean to yield to pressure or emotion. NOUN: The quality of being elastic, indicating donation or flexibility.
example: Please give me a minute to finish this task, and remember to give credit where it's due.

definition: ADJECTIVE, NOUN ADJECTIVE: Having lived or existed for only a short time; not old. Can refer to someone in an early stage of development or a new period. NOUN: Young people collectively; offspring.
example: The young artist showed great promise, creating beautiful paintings despite being so young.

definition: ADJECTIVE, PRONOUN, ADVERB ADJECTIVE: Identical; not different. PRONOUN: The identical thing or person. ADVERB: In the same way. Often implies similarity or lack of change, indicating identity.
example: They both wore the same dress, but their opinions on the matter were not the same.

definition: ADVERB, ADJECTIVE ADVERB: Exactly; merely or only; a very short time ago. ADJECTIVE: Based on or behaving according to what is morally right or fair; deserved, indicating precision or fairness.
example: I just arrived home, and I think that was a just decision given the circumstances.

definition: VERB (past tense of 'say') The past tense and past participle of 'say'. It means to utter words, to express in words, or to state a fact or opinion. Often used to report direct or indirect speech.
example: He said he would be here by noon, and everything he said turned out to be true.

definition: ADJECTIVE, ADVERB, VERB, NOUN ADJECTIVE: Measuring a great distance from end to end; lasting for a great duration. ADVERB: For a long duration. VERB: To have a strong desire or yearning. NOUN: A long period of time.
example: It was a long journey, and she longed to be back home after such a long time away.

definition: NOUN The act or power of carefully thinking about, listening to, or watching someone or something. It implies focus, awareness, and often, consideration, indicating mental engagement.
example: Please pay close attention to the instructions, as your attention to detail is crucial for this task.

definition: POSSESSIVE DETERMINER Belonging to or associated with the speaker (first person singular). It indicates possession, relationship, or origin, used before a noun to modify it.
example: This is my book, and my favorite part is the ending.

definition: ADVERB, ADJECTIVE ADVERB: At a subsequent time; afterward. ADJECTIVE: Occurring or situated at or toward the end of a process or period. Used for time subsequent to a given moment.
example: I'll call you later to discuss the details, perhaps later this evening.

definition: VERB (past tense of 'seem') The past tense of 'seem'. To give the impression of being something or having a particular quality; to appear to be. It suggests an impression rather than a definite fact.
example: It seemed like a good idea at the time, and he seemed genuinely happy with the result.

definition: ADJECTIVE, NOUN, ADVERB ADJECTIVE: Of high quality, excellence, or desirability; morally right or virtuous; beneficial. NOUN: That which is morally right or beneficial. ADVERB: (informal) well.
example: She did a good job on the project, and her efforts contributed to the greater good of the team.

definition: PRONOUN The reflexive form of 'they' or 'them', used when 'they' or 'them' is the object of a verb or preposition and also its subject. It can also be used for emphasis.
example: They built the house themselves, and they were very proud of themselves for doing it.

definition: NOUN, VERB NOUN: A faculty by which the body perceives an external stimulus (e.g., sight, smell); a feeling; practical judgment. VERB: To perceive something by a sense; to detect or become aware of.
example: She has a good sense of humor, and she could sense that something was wrong.

definition: NOUN, VERB (present participle of 'make') NOUN: The process of producing or creating something. VERB: Present participle of 'make', meaning to create, construct, cause to be, or achieve.
example: The making of this film took years, and they are now making plans for the sequel.

definition: ADVERB, PREPOSITION, ADJECTIVE ADVERB/PREPOSITION: Away from a place or position; indicating separation or disconnection. ADJECTIVE: Not operating; not fresh. Can also indicate a starting point or a period of absence.
example: He took the cap off the bottle and then headed off on his journey.

definition: VERB (past tense of 'come') The past tense of 'come'. It means to move towards or arrive at a place or a particular state. It indicates an action of approach or arrival that happened in the past.
example: She came home early yesterday, and the idea for the project just came to her.

definition: NOUN The act of enticing someone into sexual activity. More broadly, the action of attracting someone to a belief or course of action that is inadvisable or immoral, often through charm or persuasion.
example: The seduction of power can lead to corruption, but she resisted the seduction of wealth.

definition: PREPOSITION (French origin, part of names) A French preposition meaning 'of' or 'from,' often used in names (e.g., 'Joan of Arc' as 'Jeanne d'Arc'). It is not typically used as a standalone English word with a general dictionary definition beyond its etymological origin.
example: Louis de Bourbon was a prominent figure in French history, known for his noble lineage.

definition: NOUN The expression or application of human creative skill and imagination, typically in a visual form such as painting or sculpture, producing works to be appreciated primarily for their beauty or emotional power. Also, a skill.
example: Modern art can be challenging, but the art of negotiation is a crucial skill in business.

definition: DETERMINER, PRONOUN DETERMINER: One more; an additional; a different one. PRONOUN: An additional or different person or thing. It implies singularity and distinctness from what has been mentioned.
example: Can I have another cup of coffee? I need another few minutes to finish this.

definition: NOUN, VERB NOUN: The power to influence or direct people's behavior or the course of events; a means of regulating. VERB: To determine the behavior or supervise the running of; to limit or restrict.
example: She has excellent control over her emotions, and the remote control allows her to change channels easily.

definition: MODAL VERB Used to indicate obligation, duty, or correctness, suggesting what is advisable. It can also express probability, expectation, or a conditional outcome (e.g., 'if you should call').
example: You should study for your exams, and if you should need help, just ask.

definition: VERB, NOUN VERB: To allow or permit; to cause to happen or to go. Also means to rent out property. NOUN: A stoppage or hindrance, especially in tennis, indicating permission or an obstacle.
example: Please let me know if you can come, and don't let the small obstacles stop you.

definition: PROPER NOUN, NOUN PROPER NOUN: A famous French military and political leader, Napoleon Bonaparte (1769-1821), who rose to prominence during the French Revolution. NOUN: A type of pastry with layers of puff pastry and cream.
example: Napoleon's military campaigns reshaped Europe, and I ordered a delicious Napoleon cake for dessert.

definition: NOUN A human being regarded as an individual. It emphasizes individuality and distinct identity. Can also refer to a specific role or character in a play or story, representing a human entity.
example: Every person has a unique story, and she is a very kind person.

definition: DETERMINER Used to refer to all the individual members of a set without exception. It emphasizes totality and indicates that something applies to each single unit in a group.
example: Every student must complete the assignment, and we checked every detail before submission.

definition: NOUN, VERB NOUN: The final part of something, especially a period of time, an activity, or a story. It signifies termination or conclusion. VERB: To bring or come to a final point; to stop.
example: The movie came to an end, and she felt a sense of peace at the end of a long day.

definition: VERB, NOUN VERB: To have a desire or wish for something or to do something. It expresses a need, a longing, or a preference. NOUN: A lack or deficiency of something desired or needed.
example: I want to learn a new language, but I also want to finish my current projects.

definition: VERB To form or have a particular idea or opinion; to consider or ponder something. It involves mental activity, reflection, or the formation of judgments, indicating cognitive process.
example: I think it's important to think critically about all sources of information.

definition: ADVERB As an alternative or substitute; in place of. It is used to present a different choice or action in contrast to what was expected or previously mentioned, offering an alternative.
example: She couldn't come, so her sister went instead, and instead of complaining, he accepted the change.

definition: CONJUNCTION, NOUN, VERB CONJUNCTION: At the same time that; during the time that; whereas. NOUN: A period of time. VERB: To pass time, especially in a relaxed way (e.g., 'while away the hours').
example: While I was waiting, I read a book, and it took a while to finish it.

definition: ADVERB, CONJUNCTION ADVERB: In whatever way; by whatever means; nevertheless; despite this. CONJUNCTION: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or seems to contradict something previously said.
example: It was a difficult task; however, she managed to complete it successfully.

definition: NOUN An adult female human being. It emphasizes gender and often refers to a female person in general, or in specific roles or characteristics, indicating a female individual.
example: The woman in the red dress sang beautifully, and she was a strong, independent woman.

definition: VERB, NOUN, INTERJECTION VERB: To direct one's gaze in a specified direction; to appear or seem. NOUN: An act of looking; an appearance or expression. INTERJECTION: Used to draw attention.
example: Look at the beautiful sunset; it looks like a painting.

definition: VERB, NOUN VERB: To have or retain possession of; to continue to have or hold. Can also mean to maintain a state, to store, or to fulfill a promise. NOUN: A strong tower or dungeon.
example: Please keep the change, and try to keep calm under pressure.

definition: PRONOUN All things; all the things of a group or type. It denotes totality or the complete set of something. Often used to convey completeness or inclusion.
example: He lost everything in the fire, but he still had his family, which meant everything to him.

definition: PRONOUN, ADVERB, NOUN PRONOUN: Not anything; no thing. ADVERB: Not at all. NOUN: A thing of no importance or value. It denotes absence or insignificance.
example: There was nothing left in the fridge, and he said nothing about his plans.

definition: VERB (past tense of 'become') The past tense of 'become'. It means to have grown into or assumed a particular state or condition, or to have come into existence as something new.
example: She became a successful doctor, and her hard work became an inspiration to others.

definition: VERB, NOUN VERB: To employ something for a purpose; to apply something for a specific function. NOUN: The action of using something or the state of being used; purpose or advantage.
example: We need to use renewable energy sources for a better future, and the use of technology has transformed education.

definition: ADVERB After a long time, typically when there has been difficulty or delay; ultimately. It indicates the conclusion of a series of actions or events, or a conclusive point.
example: After many attempts, he finally succeeded, and the truth was finally revealed.

definition: VERB, NOUN VERB: To require something because it is essential or very important. NOUN: A requirement; something necessary for survival or well-being; a state of deprivation.
example: I need more time to finish this project, and there's a great need for more volunteers.

definition: VERB To give the impression of being something or having a particular quality; to appear to be. It expresses an impression rather than a confirmed fact, often indicating uncertainty.
example: It doesn't seem like a good idea right now, but things often seem different later.

definition: ADJECTIVE, ADVERB, DETERMINER, NOUN ADJECTIVE: Small in size, amount, or degree; brief. ADVERB: To a small extent; not much. DETERMINER: A small amount of. NOUN: A small amount or quantity.
example: She made a little progress each day, and there's little doubt that she will succeed.

definition: VERB To have information, understanding, or skill as a result of experience or education; to be aware of. It implies familiarity, recognition, or certainty, indicating acquired comprehension.
example: I know how to play the guitar, and I know that she will be a great leader.

definition: PRONOUN The objective case of 'I', referring to the speaker. It functions as the object of a verb or preposition, or sometimes as a subjective complement in informal contexts.
example: Please tell me what you think, and give me a chance to explain.

definition: NOUN, VERB, ADVERB NOUN: A piece or segment of something larger; a role in a play or activity; a component. VERB: To divide or separate; to go away from. ADVERB: Partly.
example: This is an important part of the project, and I will play my part in completing it.

definition: ADVERB, ADJECTIVE ADVERB: At, to, or by a great distance; to a great extent. ADJECTIVE: Distant in space or time; extensive. Often implies remoteness or a large difference.
example: The station is quite far from here, and so far, everything is going according to plan.

definition: VERB To bring something into existence; to cause something new to happen or exist. It implies originality, imagination, or the act of establishing something.
example: Artists create beauty from their imagination, and we hope to create new opportunities for everyone.

definition: ADVERB, CONJUNCTION ADVERB: Up until the present or a specified time; still; even now. CONJUNCTION: Nevertheless; but. It indicates something that has not happened but is expected, or introduces a contrast.
example: The package hasn't arrived yet, yet I remain hopeful.

definition: ADVERB, ADJECTIVE ADVERB: To or at a distance from a particular place, person, or thing; in a different direction. ADJECTIVE: Absent; distant. Often implies removal or absence.
example: She moved away from the city, and the children were playing away from the main road.

definition: VERB (past tense of 'know') The past tense of 'know'. It means to have had information, understanding, or familiarity with something or someone in the past. It signifies prior knowledge or recognition.
example: She knew the answer all along, but I never knew how she managed it.

definition: VERB (past tense of 'go') The past tense of 'go'. It means moved from one place to another; proceeded or traveled. It indicates a past action of movement or transition.
example: They went to the market yesterday, and the meeting went well.

definition: MODAL VERB + ADVERB (contraction of 'can not') The contracted form of 'can not'. Used to express impossibility, inability, or prohibition. It indicates that something is not possible or not permitted.
example: I cannot believe how quickly time passes, and we cannot afford to lose this opportunity.

definition: VERB (past tense of 'want') The past tense of 'want'. It means had a desire or wish for something or to do something in the past. It indicates a past need, longing, or preference.
example: He wanted to travel the world, and what he wanted most was peace.

definition: ADVERB, ADJECTIVE ADVERB: To a high degree; extremely. It intensifies the meaning of an adjective or adverb. ADJECTIVE: (formal) actual; precise; sheer, emphasizing exactness or intensity.
example: The movie was very interesting, and at that very moment, the phone rang.

definition: NOUN, VERB (past tense of 'think') NOUN: An idea or opinion produced by thinking, or the process of thinking. VERB: The past tense and past participle of 'think', meaning considered, believed, or reflected.
example: Her initial thought was to refuse, but then she thought it over and changed her mind.

definition: NOUN. A very brief period of time; an exact or specific point in time; also, a situation or opportunity of importance or significance.
example: I'll be back in a moment; this is a significant moment for our team.

definition: PREPOSITION/ADVERB. In a position directly below; less than (a specified number or amount); subject to the authority, control, or supervision of; undergoing a process.
example: The cat is hiding under the bed, currently under observation by the children.

definition: NOUN. Units of language that carry meaning; a promise or assurance; the text or lyrics of a song or speech.
example: His words of encouragement meant a lot, even though they were just a few simple words.

definition: ADJECTIVE. Having great power or strength; having a strong effect on people's feelings or thoughts; very influential or effective.
example: The powerful storm left a trail of destruction, demonstrating its powerful force.

definition: MODAL VERB/NOUN. (Modal Verb) Expressing possibility or permission, or a polite suggestion. (Noun) Great power, strength, or force.
example: He might come to the party later, as he possesses great might when it comes to organizing events.

definition: ADVERB. In a short time; before long; quickly or promptly.
example: We hope to see you again soon, and the package will arrive soon.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) A sustained fight between large organized armed forces; a long and difficult struggle. (Verb) To fight or struggle tenaciously against something.
example: The soldiers prepared for the fierce battle, knowing they would have to battle bravely against the enemy.

definition: ADJECTIVE/ADVERB/VERB/NOUN. (Adj/Adv) Of a higher standard or quality; more appealing, effective, or suitable. (Verb) To improve or surpass. (Noun) Something superior.
example: She felt much better after resting, and her performance became even better with practice.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) Strength or energy as an attribute of physical action or movement; coercion or compulsion; an organized body of armed personnel. (Verb) To make someone do something by use of strength or power.
example: The police used force to control the crowd, forcing them to disperse.

definition: VERB/NOUN. (Verb) Engage in activity for enjoyment and recreation; take part in a game; perform a dramatic role. (Noun) Activity for enjoyment; a dramatic performance.
example: Children love to play in the park, and tonight we are going to see a play at the theater.

definition: ADVERB. Another time; once more; back into a previous condition or place; in addition to what has already been done.
example: Please say that again, I didn't hear you clearly, and let's try this exercise again.

definition: VERB/NOUN. (Verb) Change physical position; progress or develop; cause deep emotional effect. (Noun) An act of moving; a deliberate action or maneuver.
example: He made a decisive move in the game, and then decided to move to a new city for work.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN/ADVERB. (Determiner/Pronoun) As much or as many as required; sufficient. (Adverb) To the necessary degree or extent; adequately.
example: Do we have enough time to finish, or have you had enough food for today?

definition: NOUN/ADJECTIVE. (Noun) A surface or line bounding an object; a particular aspect or quality; one of two or more opposing groups or points of view. (Adj) Situated at the side of.
example: He stood by her side throughout the difficult time, looking at the bright side of things.

definition: NOUN/PRONOUN/PREFIX. (Noun) A person's essential being that distinguishes them from others. (Pronoun) Used reflexively (e.g., myself, himself). (Prefix) Of oneself or itself.
example: She needs to focus on her self-improvement, and understanding oneself is crucial for growth.

definition: ADJECTIVE/ADVERB/NOUN. (Adj) Immediately following in time or order; adjacent. (Adv) Immediately after. (Noun) The person or thing immediately following.
example: What's the next step in our plan, and who is next in line?

definition: VERB. Move to or place in a particular position; express in a specified way; cause (someone or something) to be in a particular state or condition.
example: Please put the books on the shelf, and let's put our efforts into this project.

definition: NOUN. A thing that is known or proved to be true; reality or truth; information presented as objectively real.
example: It's a known fact that the Earth revolves around the sun, and in fact, it's a scientific reality.

definition: NOUN. (Plural of idea) Thoughts or suggestions about a possible course of action; concepts or impressions; mental images or representations.
example: We need some fresh ideas for the project, and her creative ideas always impress everyone.

definition: VERB/NOUN. (Verb) Past tense of 'see', meaning perceived with the eyes. (Noun) A tool with a long, thin, toothed blade used for cutting.
example: I saw a beautiful bird in the garden this morning, and he used a saw to cut the wood.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN/ADVERB. (Determiner/Pronoun) A smaller amount of; not as much. (Adverb) To a smaller extent or degree.
example: You should eat less sugar, and surprisingly, the project took less time than expected.

definition: ADJECTIVE/NOUN/PREPOSITION/ADVERB. (Adj) Gone by in time; previous. (Noun) The time that has gone by. (Prep) Beyond in time or space. (Adv) So as to pass by.
example: In the past, people used to travel by horse, and he walked right past me without noticing.

definition: NOUN. A current medium of exchange in the form of coins and banknotes, universally accepted as a means of payment; wealth or financial resources.
example: He needs money to buy food, and saving money is a good habit for the future.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) A change that is a result or consequence of an action or other cause; an impression produced. (Verb) To cause (something) to happen; bring about.
example: The new policy had a positive effect on the economy, and the team worked to effect change within the company.

definition: VERB. Past tense of 'take', meaning carried or brought; accepted; required (time or effort); understood or interpreted.
example: She took her umbrella because it looked like rain, and it took a lot of effort to complete the task.

definition: ADJECTIVE. Having the power, skill, or means to do something; capable of doing something; competent or proficient.
example: She is able to speak three languages fluently, and he was able to complete the work on time.

definition: ADJECTIVE/ADVERB/NOUN. (Adj/Adv) Of the most excellent or highest quality; most skillfully or effectively. (Noun) That which is the most excellent or outstanding.
example: This is the best book I've ever read, and she always tries her best in everything she does.

definition: ADJECTIVE. Not the same as another or each other; distinct or separate; unusual or unconventional.
example: They have very different opinions on the matter, and we tried a different approach this time.

definition: ADJECTIVE/NOUN. (Adj) Affecting or concerning most people, places, or things; not specific or specialized; prevalent. (Noun) A commander of an army; a high-ranking military officer.
example: The general public expressed a general concern about the new law, and the General commanded his troops wisely.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end; a natural or involuntary sequence of changes. (Verb) To perform a series of mechanical or chemical operations on something.
example: Learning a new language is a slow process that requires daily practice, and the factory processes raw materials into finished goods.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) The sharp or tapered end of something; a particular spot, position, or moment; a particular matter or idea. (Verb) To direct attention to something with one's finger or another object; to aim.
example: What's the main point of your argument, and can you point me in the right direction?

definition: ADJECTIVE/NOUN. (Adj) Relating to France, its language, or its culture. (Noun) The Romance language spoken in France and other countries; the people of France.
example: She is learning French to visit France next year, and French cuisine is renowned worldwide.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) An unpleasant emotion caused by the threat of danger, pain, or harm; a feeling of dread or respect. (Verb) To be afraid of (someone or something); to consider with apprehension.
example: Overcoming fear is essential for growth, and he fears public speaking more than anything.

definition: ADJECTIVE/NOUN. (Adj) Of or concerning the people as a whole; open to general view or access; for the community. (Noun) The community as a whole; a specific group of people.
example: The public expressed its opinion on the matter, and the event was open to the public.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) A strong feeling of wanting something or wishing for something to happen; a longing or craving. (Verb) To strongly wish for or want (something).
example: Her strong desire to succeed motivated her, and she truly desired a peaceful resolution to the conflict.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) A place where someone or something is located or has been put; a job or role; an opinion or stance. (Verb) To put (someone or something) in a particular place or arrangement.
example: Her position as a manager gives her a lot of responsibility, and he positioned the camera to get the best shot.

definition: VERB/NOUN. (Verb) Past tense of 'feel', meaning perceived through the sense of touch or general sensation; experienced an emotion or a belief. (Noun) A type of non-woven cloth.
example: She felt a strange vibration in the ground, and I felt it was important to share my honest opinion.

definition: ADJECTIVE/ADVERB. (Adj) Solid, firm, and resistant to pressure; difficult or demanding; severe or strict. (Adv) With great effort or intensity; strenuously.
example: It's hard to break this rock, but he worked hard to achieve his goals despite the difficulties.

definition: PREPOSITION/ADVERB. (Prep) At, in, or to the space separating two or more points, objects, or people; in the interval separating two points in time or events; indicating a relationship or comparison. (Adv) In the intervening space or time.
example: The secret was shared between the two friends, and the meeting is scheduled between 2 and 3 PM.

definition: VERB/NOUN. (Verb) Take part in a violent struggle involving physical force; contend with difficulties or opposition. (Noun) A violent confrontation or struggle; an argument.
example: They had a big fight over a misunderstanding, but they vowed to fight for their rights.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) An aggressive and violent act against a person or place; a sudden onset of an illness. (Verb) To take aggressive action against (a place or person); to criticize or challenge forcefully.
example: The enemy launched a surprise attack at dawn, causing the general to attack the problem from a different angle.

definition: VERB. Past tense of 'find', meaning discovered or located unexpectedly or after a search. Also, the base form of the verb 'to found', meaning to establish or set up (an institution or organization).
example: She found her lost keys under the couch, and the organization was founded in 1950 to support local artists.

definition: ADJECTIVE/ADVERB/NOUN/VERB. (Adj) Morally good, justified, or acceptable; correct or true; on the side of the body facing east when one is facing north. (Adv) Exactly; correctly. (Noun) A moral or legal entitlement; the right-hand side. (Verb) Restore to a proper position.
example: You have the right to express your opinion, and please turn right at the next intersection.

definition: ADVERB/ADJECTIVE/NOUN/VERB. (Adv) Continuing up to the present time; nevertheless. (Adj) Not moving or making a sound; calm. (Noun) Deep silence and inactivity. (Verb) Make or become still.
example: It's still raining outside, but the lake is perfectly still this morning, reflecting the sky.

definition: VERB/ADJECTIVE/NOUN. (Verb) Past tense of 'leave', meaning departed from, or remained. (Adj) On the side of the body that is to the west when one is facing north; remaining. (Noun) The left-hand side.
example: He left his keys on the table, and there was only one slice of pizza left.

definition: PREPOSITION/ADVERB/CONJUNCTION. (Prep) In the intervening period between (a time or event) and the time under consideration. (Adv) From that time until now. (Conj) From the time when; because; seeing that.
example: I haven't seen her since last year, and since you're here, let's discuss the plan.

definition: NOUN/ADJECTIVE. (Noun) The process of considering or reasoning about something; the activity of using one's mind. (Adj) Using one's mind to consider or reason; thoughtful.
example: His critical thinking skills are impressive, and I need some time for quiet thinking before I decide.

definition: ADVERB. Used to express uncertainty or possibility; maybe; by chance.
example: Perhaps we should take a different route, or perhaps it will rain later today.

definition: PREPOSITION/ADVERB. (Prep) Inside (something); not beyond the limits of (a particular area, scope, or period); inside the range or boundaries of. (Adv) Inside or internally.
example: The answer can be found within the pages of this book, and the project needs to be completed within a week.

definition: NOUN. The action or fact of dying or being killed; the permanent end of life in a person or animal; the end or destruction of something.
example: The death of the old tree left a void in the garden, marking the end of an era.

definition: ADVERB. At any time; at all times; always; in any way; by any means (often used for emphasis).
example: Have you ever visited that city, and she's more beautiful than ever before?

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN/CONJUNCTION. (Determiner/Pronoun) Referring to two people or things, regarded together. (Conj) Used with 'and' to emphasize that two things are true or apply.
example: Both options are good, and she is both intelligent and kind.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) The end part of a person's arm, beyond the wrist, including the palm and fingers; a side or direction; assistance. (Verb) To pass or give (something) to someone.
example: Please give me a hand with this heavy box, and he held her hand as they walked.

definition: VERB. Present participle of 'have', meaning possessing or owning; experiencing; being in the state of; used to form perfect tenses.
example: Having completed the project, she felt a sense of relief, and having good friends is a true blessing.

definition: NOUN. (Plural of enemy) People who are actively opposed or hostile to someone or something; opposing forces or groups.
example: In times of war, former allies can become bitter enemies, but they tried to turn their enemies into friends.

definition: VERB. To acquire knowledge of or skill in something through study, experience, or teaching; to be informed of or find out.
example: Children learn quickly when they are engaged, and I need to learn how to cook this dish.

definition: ADJECTIVE/ADVERB. (Adj) Actually existing as a thing or occurring in fact; not imagined or supposed; true and authentic. (Adv) Very; extremely (informal).
example: Is that a real diamond, or is it just a very real-looking fake?

definition: NOUN. (Plural of woman) Adult female human beings; female persons collectively.
example: The conference brought together women leaders from around the world, celebrating their achievements.

definition: ADJECTIVE/NOUN. (Adj) Able to be done or achieved; capable of happening or being true; within the bounds of possibility. (Noun) A possible candidate or option.
example: It's possible that it will rain tomorrow, and we must do everything possible to prevent it.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) The visible shape or configuration of something; a type or kind; a document with spaces for information. (Verb) To make or fashion into a certain shape or style; to establish or develop.
example: Water can take many forms: solid, liquid, and gas, and they decided to form a new committee.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) A number of people or things that are located, gathered, or classified together; a set. (Verb) To put into a group or groups; to form a group.
example: A small group of students met to discuss the project, and they decided to group the tasks by priority.

definition: ADJECTIVE/NOUN. (Adj) Having lived or existed for a long time; of a specified age; having existed for a long time. (Noun) A person or thing of a specified age or from an earlier time.
example: My grandmother is 90 years old, and this is an old family tradition that we cherish.

definition: VERB/NOUN. (Verb) To make it easier for (someone) to do something by offering one's services or resources; to improve (a situation or problem). (Noun) The action of helping someone; assistance.
example: Can you help me carry these bags, and your help with the report was invaluable?

definition: NOUN. An emotional state or reaction; a belief or opinion, especially one not based on facts; an ability to experience sensation; a physical sensation.
example: I had a strange feeling that something good would happen, and she expressed her true feelings about the situation.

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN/ADVERB. (Determiner) Every one of two or more people or things, regarded separately. (Pronoun) Each one. (Adverb) Each to or for the other; apiece.
example: Each student received a certificate, and they greeted each other warmly.

definition: VERB/NOUN/ADJECTIVE. (Verb) Put, lay, or stand (something) in a specified place; adjust (a device); cause to do something. (Noun) A group of similar things; a collection of equipment; a theatrical scene. (Adj) Fixed or established; ready.
example: Please set the table for dinner, and we need a complete set of tools for this job.

definition: VERB/NOUN. (Verb) Move in a circular direction around an axis; change direction; become (a specified age or condition). (Noun) An act of turning; a change in direction; an opportunity or obligation.
example: It's your turn to play the game, and please turn off the lights when you leave.

definition: ADVERB. Very nearly; all but; not quite.
example: We're almost home, and she almost forgot her keys this morning.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) A particular position, point, or area in space; a city, town, or village; a position in a hierarchy or ranking. (Verb) To put in a particular position; to identify or classify.
example: This is a beautiful place to live, and please place the documents on my desk.

definition: NOUN. A country in Western Europe, known for its rich history, culture, and cuisine, with Paris as its capital.
example: France is known for its rich history and exquisite cuisine, attracting tourists from all over the world.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) The front part of a person's head from the forehead to the chin; the surface of something. (Verb) To be positioned with the face towards (someone or something); to confront or deal with.
example: She had a smile on her face despite the difficulties she had to face.

definition: VERB/ADJECTIVE. (Verb) Past tense of 'decide', meaning made a choice or resolution. (Adj) Clear and definite; unequivocal.
example: They decided to go on a trip to the mountains, and she had a decided advantage in the competition.

definition: NOUN/VERB/ADJECTIVE. (Noun) A skilled practitioner of an art or activity; a person in control; an owner or employer. (Verb) To acquire complete knowledge or skill in something; to gain control of. (Adj) Having or showing great skill.
example: He is a master of several martial arts, and he quickly mastered the new software.

definition: ADVERB. Preferably; to a certain extent; somewhat (often used to express a slight contrast or to qualify a statement); instead.
example: I'd rather stay home tonight than go out, and it's rather cold for this time of year.

definition: NOUN. The phenomena of the physical world collectively, including plants, animals, the landscape, and other features not made by humans; the essential qualities or characteristics of a person or thing.
example: Spending time in nature can be very calming, and it's not in his nature to be unkind.

definition: NOUN. (Plural of eye) The organs of sight in humans and animals; a person's ability to see; a particular way of looking at something.
example: She closed her eyes and took a deep breath, and he has a keen eye for detail.

definition: PRONOUN. An unspecified person; some person.
example: Someone left the door open, and I hope someone can help me with this problem.

definition: PRONOUN. (Reflexive) Used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to a thing or animal previously mentioned. (Emphatic) Used to emphasize a particular thing or animal.
example: The cat cleaned itself thoroughly, and the city itself is quite beautiful.

definition: VERB/NOUN. (Verb) To allow or enable to be seen; to point out or explain; to demonstrate. (Noun) A theatrical or broadcast performance; an exhibition or display.
example: Can you show me how to use this machine, and the art show features works by local artists?

definition: DETERMINER/PRONOUN. More than two but not many; an indefinite number of.
example: She bought several books at the fair, and I have several reasons for my decision.

definition: PRONOUN/ADVERB. (Pronoun) A thing of any kind; whatever thing. (Adverb) At all (used for emphasis, especially in questions or negative statements).
example: Do you need anything from the store, or anything at all?

definition: NOUN. (Plural of day) Periods of 24 hours from one midnight to the next; periods of time, especially considered with regard to their characteristic events or circumstances.
example: The hot summer days are finally over, and in those days, life was simpler.

definition: VERB/NOUN. (Verb) To utter words; express (an idea or opinion); assume or suppose. (Noun) An opportunity to speak or express an opinion; an influence.
example: What did you say, and do you have any say in the decision-making process?

definition: ADJECTIVE/PRONOUN. (Adj) Known for sure; established beyond doubt; sure to happen; identified but not named specifically. (Pronoun) Certain ones (of a group).
example: I'm certain she will succeed, and a certain amount of risk is involved in any investment.

definition: NOUN. A large town; an important centre of commerce, population, or culture.
example: New York City is a bustling metropolis, and she dreams of living in a big city.

definition: VERB/ADJECTIVE. (Verb) Present participle of 'try', meaning making an effort to do something; testing or examining. (Adj) Difficult or annoying; demanding.
example: He is trying his best to learn English, and it has been a very trying time for everyone.

definition: PRONOUN. Every person; all people.
example: Everyone is invited to the party, and everyone needs to do their part.

definition: NOUN. The state of things as they actually exist, as opposed to an idealistic or notional idea of them; the world or the universe as experienced.
example: She struggled to face the reality of the situation, and virtual reality games are becoming very popular.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) A man in relation to his natural child or children; a male parent; an originator or founder. (Verb) To be the father of (a child).
example: My father taught me how to ride a bicycle, and he is often considered the father of modern physics.

definition: VERB. Past tense of 'give', meaning freely transferred the possession of (something) to (someone); provided or supplied; caused to have or experience.
example: She gave him a present for his birthday, and the teacher gave us homework.

definition: NOUN/VERB. (Noun) A thing done; a deed; a division of a play or opera; a law. (Verb) To take action; perform a role in a play or film; behave in a specified way.
example: It was an act of kindness to help the stranger, and the actors will act out the scene tonight.

definition: ADJECTIVE/NOUN. (Adj) Relating to or characteristic of humankind. (Noun) A human being; a person.
example: We should treat all human beings with respect, as it's a fundamental human right.

definition: VERB. To take or go with (someone or something) to a place; to cause to come into a particular state or condition; to lead to.
example: Please bring your books to class, and this decision could bring about significant changes.

definition: ADVERB. Quickly and unexpectedly; all of a sudden.
example: The lights suddenly went out, plunging the room into darkness.
